title: P0-2r cli-retry-analysis: Fix analyze_retry to return can_retry=false for RunCancelled runs
description: Bug P0-2r (revision of black-hat-rejected vb-5rg5y). Black-hat review round 1 found that cmd_retry IS already wired to lifecycle::retry at run_ops.rs:25 (the original 'no-op' framing was fabricated). The real bug is in crates/vb_cli/src/commands_journal.rs:351-353 where analyze_retry returns can_retry: true for RunCancelled runs. The function checks `is_failed` (RunFailedEvent | RunCancelled) and exits early only on the negation; once the run is failed/cancelled, the function returns can_retry: true unconditionally. The fix is a one-liner: when the terminal event is RunCancelled, return can_retry: false with reason 'run was cancelled, not failed; use submit to restart'. When terminal is RunFailedEvent, keep can_retry: true. This bead does NOT touch run_ops.rs (the wiring is already correct). Master §33.3 lifecycle: retry is for failed runs; cancelled runs require explicit submit. Kani harness: prove analyze_retry({...RunCancelled...}) -> can_retry == false. proptest: 100 random journal sequences with terminal in {Finished, Failed, Cancelled, Succeeded, None} all return correct can_retry.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL return can_retry=false from analyze_retry when the run was cancelled, not failed
THE SYSTEM SHALL preserve existing analyze_retry behavior for the RunFailedEvent terminal case

event_driven.trigger: WHEN analyze_retry is called with a journal ending in RunCancelled
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL return RetryAnalysis { can_retry: false, reason: 'run was cancelled, not failed; use submit to restart', .. }

event_driven.trigger: WHEN analyze_retry is called with a journal ending in RunFailedEvent
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL return RetryAnalysis { can_retry: true, failed_at_step: Some(step), .. } (preserved behavior)

unwanted.condition: IF the journal is empty or non-terminal
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT return can_retry: true; the existing 'no retry needed' early-return is correct
unwanted.because: Preserves the existing happy-path behavior and is the current contract

JournalEvent::RunCancelled is a distinct variant from RunFailedEvent

analyze_retry on RunFailedEvent journal still returns can_retry=true (regression-protected)
No other analyze_retry behavior changes; the failure_step calculation is preserved

For any journal whose terminal event is RunFailedEvent, analyze_retry returns can_retry=true (regression-protected)
